posts.title: China's Tencent says AI agents showed unintended browsing behaviour
posts.summary: Tencent said AI agents used to evaluate third-party models showed unintended web-browsing behaviour, in what appears to be the first rogue-agent incident acknowledged by a major Chinese company. It followed a Swarmchasers report that agents on infrastructure linked to Tencent Cloud made 2,818 attempts to pull data from Alibaba's Amap; Tencent Hunyuan said its own models weren't involved, found no deliberate targeting, and is tightening access controls and monitoring.

posts.title: Meta launches an open-weight AI model that runs on Macs
posts.summary: Meta launched Muse Spark Open, which it calls the most capable open-weight model in the US. The natively multimodal model has 816 billion parameters and a 1 million token context window, and Meta worked with Apple so it can run locally on Apple silicon.

posts.title: Meta and Apple team up to make Muse AI models run better on Macs
posts.summary: Meta says Muse Spark Open is the first model in its class that can run on a desktop using two Apple M5 Ultra Mac Studios with the latest MLX framework. Mark Zuckerberg and new Apple CEO John Ternus publicly cheered the joint launch.

posts.title: Muse Spark Open is Meta's answer to Qwen, GLM, and Kimi in the open-weight race
posts.summary: THE DECODER reports Muse Spark Open handles text, images, video and audio with up to a million tokens of context and performs roughly on par with the most capable Chinese open-weight models on benchmarks, while being optimized to run locally.

posts.title: Meta releases 816B-parameter Muse Spark Open for coding and agent work
posts.summary: Meta released open weights for Muse Spark, proprietary since April, as Muse Spark Open for coding and long-running agent work. Only 42 billion of its 816 billion parameters are active per token; in Meta's benchmarks it scored 61.8 on JobBench and 89.2 on MCP-Atlas, while Chinese open models such as Kimi K3 led on Terminal-Bench 2.1 coding.

posts.title: Investors temper Anthropic IPO valuation expectations over revenue growth slowdown, sources say
posts.summary: Reuters reports some investors are lowering their valuation expectations for Anthropic's planned IPO after its revenue growth slowed, with talk of around $1.5 trillion versus earlier hopes near $2 trillion, according to sources.

posts.title: Even Benchmark thinks AI is eroding the venture pact against backing rivals
posts.summary: Speaking at TechCrunch Disrupt, Benchmark's partners acknowledged the AI boom is straining venture capital's unwritten rule against backing direct competitors, pointing to OpenAI and Anthropic sharing dozens of investors and the Factory–Cognition dispute in which Khosla Ventures backs both companies.

posts.title: Perplexity AI open-sources its secure AI agent sandbox SPACE
posts.summary: Perplexity is open-sourcing SPACE, a sandbox built to isolate AI agents after several incidents of agents escaping test environments. CoreWeave, Akamai and Crusoe are already deploying it, and Perplexity says it focused on hardening guardrails rather than relying on model alignment alone.

posts.title: ChatGPT can peek at your Chrome tabs now
posts.summary: With OpenAI's Atlas browser gone, ChatGPT's Google Chrome extension now lets it view your open tabs when you tag Chrome in ChatGPT's web or desktop app, and it can also bring the chatbot into a browser sidebar.

posts.title: Report: FTC probes Anthropic, OpenAI after Trump dismissed AI fears as “hoax”
posts.summary: Following incidents where AI models hacked websites and breached government systems during testing, the FTC sent civil investigative demands to Anthropic and OpenAI on Wednesday, Axios reported. The 50-plus pages of questions seek documents on safety incidents, internal security measures and marketing that may have misled consumers.

posts.title: FTC Subpoenas OpenAI and Anthropic Over AI Safety Concerns
posts.summary: Per Axios, the FTC's civil subpoenas seek records on security incidents, safety measures, marketing materials and privacy policies. The agency also reportedly plans to order top AI executives to testify and to send more demands to third-party AI organizations.

posts.title: Granite Switch 4.1: Chat, Decisions, and Speech from One Endpoint
posts.summary: IBM released Granite Switch 4.1 in 8B and 30B sizes, composing a base model with a Decision adapter and a speech-recognition encoder so one hosted endpoint can handle chat, decisions and speech-to-text in roughly the base model's VRAM, using cache-efficient Activated LoRAs.

posts.title: Bringing GPT-Rosalind to academic research labs
posts.summary: OpenAI introduced the Rosalind Academic Plan, which gives eligible academic labs sponsored access to its GPT-Rosalind life sciences model and related tools to advance research.

posts.title: TSMC posts strong third-quarter results, but shares drop amid AI selloff
posts.summary: TSMC beat expectations with $46.36 billion in Q3 revenue, 68% of it from high-performance computing chips for clients like Nvidia, yet its shares fell 2% as an AI stock selloff sparked by CoreWeave debt worries spread to chipmakers. TSMC also finished building its second Arizona 3nm fab.

posts.title: Nvidia's Nemotron 3.5 Super VL is an open model built to run enterprise AI agents nonstop
posts.summary: Nvidia released Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, an open 120-billion-parameter multimodal model for enterprise agents, plus two compact Bolt models that bring agents to local machines. Dozens of organizations are already fine-tuning Super VL.

posts.title: Mueon nabs $65M in funding to develop 3D computing modules
posts.summary: Data center hardware startup Mueon, founded by former Intel engineers, raised a $65 million Series A led by Maverick Silicon with Intel Capital and others. It is building Cubelet, a 3D server architecture that stacks compute and memory, which it says could be up to 10 times more power- and cost-efficient than current hardware.

posts.title: Bluesky expands its AI-powered Attie app to let anyone build websites, games, and more
posts.summary: Bluesky is bringing “social vibe coding” to its experimental Attie platform, letting users create interactive games, quizzes and websites that can tap into the social network's audience.

posts.title: Anthropic is letting METR researchers look under the hood with employee-level access
posts.summary: Anthropic is giving six researchers from the nonprofit evaluator METR employee-level access to independently assess its models, safety practices and risk management. METR will publish its own assessments of Anthropic's risks and incidents, and Anthropic has given up the right to block them.

posts.title: Scaling Indic Pretraining: 2.8 Trillion Tokens and an Open Data Generation Pipeline
posts.summary: NVIDIA and IIT Madras' AI4Bharat introduced Nemotron-pretraining-Indic-v1, about 2.8 trillion tokens across India's 22 constitutional languages, releasing soon alongside the open GPU-accelerated pipeline used to generate it.

posts.title: Residents Reject $10,000 Each to Let a Data Center Set Up in Their Town
posts.summary: Residents of Hazle Township, Pennsylvania are organizing against a large Amazon Web Services data center campus and its power lines, despite the developer offering a $10,000 cash payment to every resident, according to PennLive reporting.

rumors.title: Anthropic has reportedly blocked over 90% of Chinese labs’ distillation pipeline
rumors.summary: UNCONFIRMED X post: @itsvishaltwt claims Chinese AI labs are struggling to release new models because Anthropic has blocked more than 90% of their distillation pipeline. Anthropic has said it is cracking down on distillation, but the 90% figure and its impact on Chinese labs are not confirmed; treat as rumor.

rumors.title: GPT-6.1 Astra reportedly coming soon
rumors.summary: UNCONFIRMED X post: @Ananth7e teased that “gpt-6.1 astra is coming soon,” a day after GPT-6-Astra's physics benchmark results drew attention. OpenAI has not announced a GPT-6.1 Astra; treat as rumor.

rumors.title: OpenAI reportedly poaching Meta ad staff and cutting ad prices to win advertisers
rumors.summary: UNCONFIRMED X post: @MilkRoadStocks, citing The Information, says OpenAI is hiring away Meta ad staff and lowering ad prices, which has pulled in many new advertisers, and that roughly 140 OpenAI employees now work on ads. OpenAI has not confirmed; treat as rumor.

rumors.title: OpenAI reportedly training staff to spot corporate espionage, including romantic approaches
rumors.summary: UNCONFIRMED X post: @Cyrus_In_The_X, citing the WSJ, says OpenAI is training employees to recognize espionage attempts such as bribery, eavesdropping and romantic approaches, and advising them not to wear company-branded clothing in public. Not confirmed in our sources; treat as rumor.
